## A line through two points {#fv3-two-points .fv-lesson .line-lesson}

```{=html}
<p>A line passes through the distinct points <span data-math="P"></span> and <span data-math="Q"></span>. <strong>What direction vector could describe this line?</strong></p><p>Let their position vectors be <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{p}"></span> and <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{q}"></span>.</p><div data-line-two-points></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §3.2 · pp. 38–40</div>

::: {.notes}
Pause for students to suggest a direction vector before using Show a direction vector. PQ=q−p is one choice. QP=p−q and any non-zero scalar multiple are equally valid. P and Q must be distinct. The reveal adds PQ to the diagram and gives r=p+λ(q−p). Ask why λ=0 gives P and λ=1 gives Q. Complete the reasoning with the class rather than giving a recipe.
:::
